messages.content:
Risk: Information Security
Description: Lowered barriers for offensive cyber capabilities, including via automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities to ease hacking, malware, phishing, offensive cyber operations, or other cyberattacks; increased attack surface for targeted cyberattacks, which may compromise a system’s availability or the confidentiality or integrity of training data, code, or model weights.
Concern: None
Policy: Training

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ContentSafetyHazard: Content Safety Hazard — Root class for content safety harm categories relevant to adversarial prompt generation against LLM deployments. [found by 20/67 queries]
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HarmfulHowTo: Harmful How-To — Step-by-step instructions for activities that cause property destruction, physical harm, or enable illegal intrusion when executed by unauthorized individuals. [found by 15/67 queries]
  Siblings: CBRN Information, Drug Synthesis, Dual-Use Research Concern
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Cyberterrorism: Cyberterrorism — Use of digital attacks against critical infrastructure or information systems to create fear and disruption for political ends. [found by 14/67 queries]
  Siblings: International Terrorism, Domestic Terrorism
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 9/67 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#LockPickingAndBypassing: Lock Picking and Bypassing — Detailed techniques for defeating physical security locks, alarms, or access controls to enable unauthorized entry into protected spaces. [found by 9/67 queries]
  Siblings: Arson Methods, Sabotage Instructions

axes.rationale: Cyberterrorism involves the use of digital attacks, which are directly relevant to the risk of information security, including hacking, malware, phishing, and other cyberattacks.

Dangerous Information includes knowledge or instructions that can enable harmful activities, which is pertinent to the risk of information security, as it can compromise the confidentiality or integrity of training data, code, or model weights.
